panels.visual: The great city of Alexandria in Egypt with the lighthouse and the library, a clear banner reading ALEXANDRIA, EGYPT
panels.caption: Hypatia lived and taught in Alexandria, in Egypt. Not in Athens.

panels.visual: Hypatia lecturing with an astrolabe and scrolls to an attentive crowd of students from far away
panels.caption: Around AD 400 she taught mathematics, astronomy and Plato's philosophy.

panels.visual: Hypatia driving her own chariot through Alexandria's busy street, people watching with admiration and tension
panels.caption: She drove her own chariot and lectured in public.

panels.visual: A quiet, sad panel: an astrolabe and a few broken pottery shards (ostraka) lying on a church floor, a dark crowd's silhouettes at the edge of the frame; no violence shown
panels.caption: In AD 415 she was killed by a mob. A Christian historian condemned it.
